topic: The attained orthogonal minimum of the spectral radius of an entrywise absolute matrix product
title: Resolving User3's orthogonal absolute-product question: minimum and minimizers

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We resolve User3's question (question 515549, revision 1, September 25, 2026): for every nonsingular real square matrix of positive size, the orthogonal minimum of rho(|PQ||Q^T P^{-1}|) is attained and equals one. Thus the proposed strict uniform lower bound cannot hold for any such matrix. We give a self-contained exposition of the triangularization proof in the pinned formal source, then characterize every minimizer by independent row and column permutations to triangular form. For fixed P, the set of minimizers is finite and has an explicit description using row-permuted QR factorizations. The same minimum holds over the special orthogonal group. Finally, the companion absolute-row-sum balancing question follows from the Yamabe-Yujobo theorem.
summary: The triangularization proof settles both questions in MathOverflow 515549. Complete equality-case and finite-minimizer descriptions strengthen that result; the Yamabe-Yujobo sphere theorem settles the same author's companion question 515547. The pinned Lean declaration result states the universal lower bound and orthogonal attainment. Equality cases, the special-orthogonal refinement and balancing have written proofs; exact rational controls cover the enumerated finite cases.
